chunks.title: Vitreous anatomy & how to look at it
chunks.tldr: Collagen fibre scaffold + hyaluronan gel. Cortex touches lens anteriorly and retina posteriorly. Strongest attachment: vitreous base (straddles ora, never detaches); also disc, macula, vessels. Age/myopia/blood/inflammation → collagen cross-linking and contraction → PVD; saccade-driven dynamic traction tears the retina at sticky spots. Cell invasion (RPE, glia) → static traction RD without tears. Examine with narrow off-axis slit + contact lens, indirect ophthalmoscope; opaque media → B-scan; macula interface → OCT.
points: 'Vitreous bands' are usually just the posterior hyaloid; true bands follow penetrating trauma or Toxocara.
chunks.hook: The gel never lets go of its base — that's where tears happen.

cards.a: The vitreous base (spanning the ora serrata) — it never separates.

chunks.title: Floaters, flashes & PVD
chunks.tldr: PVD in ≥70% of people; causes most floaters (rings = Weiss ring from disc attachment) and photopsia (mechanical retinal traction, worse on eye movement). Any new floaters or flashes → dilated indirect exam of the periphery within days. Vitreous haemorrhage → find the source (torn vessel, PDR, RVO, sickle, leukaemia); cells → think lymphoma, sarcoid, Candida. Asteroid hyalosis: golden calcium-lipid spheres, no visual effect, no diabetes link. Vitrectomy/YAG for floaters rarely justified.
points: Migraine aura: bilateral jagged scintillating scotoma (may have no headache) — not photopsia.
chunks.hook: New floaters + flashes = look for a tear before you reassure.

cards.q: Is asteroid hyalosis associated with diabetes?
cards.a: No — this old teaching has been disproved; it rarely affects vision.

chunks.title: Vitreomacular disease
chunks.tldr: OCT is the key test. Epimacular membrane: glial cells grow through a defect after PVD → contraction, metamorphopsia; Rx vitrectomy + membrane peel ± ILM peel. Vitreomacular traction: taut adherent hyaloid lifts the fovea; vitrectomy. Macular hole: OCT decides partial vs full thickness; full-thickness → vitrectomy + ILM peel + SF6 gas (~90% good result); partial → observe unless symptomatic/cystic.

cards.q: Standard surgery for full-thickness macular hole?
cards.a: Pars plana vitrectomy, ILM peel and gas tamponade (SF6) ± posturing.

chunks.title: Retinal breaks, diabetes, post-cataract & trauma vitrectomy
chunks.tldr: Horseshoe (flap) tears under traction → RRD; round atrophic holes in lattice and operculated holes rarely do. PDR haemorrhage: PRP ± anti-VEGF; dense bleed → B-scan to rule out tractional RD; vitrectomy with segmentation/delamination + endolaser. Post-cataract: RRD 0.5–1% (more after capsule rupture/vitreous loss); dropped nucleus → vitrectomy + fragmentation; endophthalmitis → tap/inject ± vitrectomy. Trauma: mobile vitreous with attached retina → observe; vitrectomy ~7–10 days after repair; metallic/organic IOFB → prompt removal.
chunks.hook: Iron or copper in the eye must come out; glass may stay.

cards.q: Which retinal breaks are highest risk for RD?
cards.a: Symptomatic flap (horseshoe) tears with persistent vitreous traction.
